main_body: Flat-roofed adobe house: a sand-coloured terrace roof (rows 0-32) with a rug and a hatch, above a clay front wall (rows 33-63) with an arched door and a window
top_band: Light sand/tan roof surface with a parapet rim, rows 0-31, then a lighter front-edge row at about rows 29-31
evidence: Down the middle column there is a wide light roof surface with a raised parapet, rug and hatch, so it clearly reads as a horizontal surface seen from above. A light front-edge row (about 28-31) follows, then a dark eave row (32-34) shading the wall. The wall below has its own speckled shading, dark crenel-like notches under the eave, an arched door with a pale frame, and a window with a sill. The roof is tall for a foreshortened top, but its contents show it is a flat terrace roof and not a face. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The outlines are dark brown, tinted to the neighbouring material, so they are not sticker-like. The roof and wall carry speckle dots in 3-4 tones, and the rug, door studs and window lattice add detail. Next to the references, though, there are fewer value steps per material than the 5-6 on their tile roofs and stone. The large roof field is mostly a single sand tone with sparse speckle, and the wall is also fairly even. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the references.
